newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai stocks pare gains, end higher on budget cuts.
newsitem.headline: Thai stocks pare gains, end higher on budget cuts.

text.p: Thai stocks gained for the third consecutive trading day on Wednesday, rising 1.44 percent on heavy turnover on buying following a government decision to slash its budget in order to boost the economy, brokers said.
After rising to 848.95 early, the SET index finished 11.82 points higher to 831.93 on 7.6 billion baht turnover. The SET-50 index gained 1.07 points to 62.10.
"Surprisingly, the index rose amid market rumours in the afternoon that some financial institutions were facing growing loan defaults by borrowers," said Lan Pajasalmi of First Asia Securities.
Brokers noted that similar rumours had spread in the market several times since late last year. The rumours last surfaced in the battered market on Friday.
"The market's still very sensitive now. We don't need any bad news in the market," Lan said.

She said the volatile index ended in the positive territory because of the government's decision, announced by Finance Minister Amnuay Viravan on Tuesday, that he would cut the annual government budget by at least 50 billion baht a year in fiscal 1997 and 1998.
Brokers said investors bought blue-chip bank, communication and finance issues today.

Krung Thai Bank topped the active list, rising one baht to 51.50. National Finance and Securities gained 0.50 to 47.75 while Siam Cement, Thailand's largest cement manufacturer, advanced 44 to 808 and TelecomAsia surged three to 52.
Support is seen by some brokers at around 820 and resistance is pegged around 840 on Thursday, brokers said.
